context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter7 fix (Expo config plugin for Android gradle Metaspace + lint disable) is verified end-to-end in cloud env. The user must `git pull` and re-run `node node_modules/expo/bin/cli prebuild --platform android --clean --no-install` on Windows — the plugin will auto-apply both fixes. Android Studio Run ▶ should then succeed without the lintVitalAnalyzeRelease OOM crash. All three layers (iter5 package pins, iter6 Windows CLI fix, iter7 gradle/lint plugin) are now in place and intact.
rca of the issue: Root cause of recurring Metaspace OOM: every `expo prebuild --clean` regenerates the android/ directory from scratch, wiping any manual edits to android/gradle.properties. Combined with the slow + memory-hungry `lintVitalAnalyzeRelease` Gradle task that ships with react-native modules (like @react-native-async-storage), the default JVM heap/metaspace settings get exhausted on 8GB Windows machines. Fix: an Expo config plugin (`withAndroidBuildFixes`) hooks into the prebuild pipeline via `withGradleProperties` (to bump JVM args) and `withAppBuildGradle` (to inject a `lint { abortOnError false; checkReleaseBuilds false; disable ... }` block that skips lintVitalAnalyzeRelease entirely). The plugin runs on every prebuild, making the fix persistent across `--clean` invocations.
